I have been farming cotton in Quzhou County for ten years now, and over that time I have learned what works on my small plot. My 1.5 mu is not large, but because some of my family works off-farm, we have cash to buy good inputs, and with six people in the household we still have enough labor to manage it carefully. I grow only cotton — it is what I know, and the local buyer comes to the village every autumn.

This spring, I will sow my improved cotton variety around mid-April, after the soil warms up. I always use rotary tillage to prepare the seedbed; it is fast and leaves a fine tilth that helps the young plants emerge evenly. I will put down about 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer as a basal dressing, and then topdress with urea when the plants start flowering, bringing my total nitrogen to about 22 kg per mu. I also make sure to get some phosphorus and potassium in at planting — around 10 kg P₂O₅ and 8 kg K₂O per mu — because my soil needs it and the bolls fill better when the plants have enough nutrition early on.

Because I have a well, I do not have to wait for rain. I will irrigate three times: once right after sowing if the spring is dry, once at full bloom, and once during peak boll development. That is one more than some of my neighbors, but on only 1.5 mu the fuel cost is small and the yield gain is worth it. For pests, I keep an eye on the fields every few days. I will spray about ten times in total — mostly for bollworm, aphids, and red spider mite, and once or twice for weeds. I have done this long enough to know the signs, and I spray before the damage gets out of hand. If the weather stays favorable and I stay on top of the watering and spraying, I expect to harvest around 550 kg of seed cotton per mu by late October.
